## Done

`landing/index.html` is a single-file landing page for Piet Mondrian's *Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow* (1930). I built it from `FACTSHEET.md` only, opened it in the browser, and verified it renders end to end with no build step.

**Assumptions I made (the brief left these open):**
- "Speak Mondrian's visual language" = De Stijl Neoplasticism on the page itself: only horizontal/vertical black lines, the three primary colours, white ground, thick rules, sharp geometry, no rounded corners, no gradients, no decorative type. I applied this to the whole layout, not just an illustration.
- I used a small Three.js scene (the only CDN the brief allows) as the hero canvas to render the painting itself in 3D — a nod to the block-and-line composition. It's decorative (`aria-hidden`) and degrades silently if WebGL is unavailable; the page content stands alone without it.
- "Read more at the source the fact sheet gives" = the Wikipedia URL from the fact sheet, used as the CTA button, in-page source link, and footer.
- The page speaks in English (matching the source language) with `lang="en"`.

**What a visitor leaves knowing (all from the fact sheet, nothing beyond it):**
- **Painter:** Piet Mondrian (1872–1944), Dutch
- **Year:** 1930
- **Movement:** De Stijl, founded in the Netherlands in 1917 by Theo van Doesburg and Piet Mondrian
- **Why it matters:** its asymmetric balance of a few primary-colour blocks became a reference for modern graphic design and architecture
- **Invitation to read more:** CTA to the Wikipedia source, which also carries the alternate title *Composition II in Red, Blue, and Yellow*

**How I know it is right:**
- Read `FACTSHEET.md` and traced every factual claim on the page back to a line in it (painter, year, medium, collection, movement, founders, Neoplasticism principles, the description of the picture, why it matters). I added no external facts.

I corrected two coordinate issues in the 3D scene (block overflow, then cell placement) across two revision rounds and re-verified each time by reloading and screenshotting.
- Closed the browser tab I opened; the remaining `about:blank` tab is already closed, so no browser session is left running.

**Open limits:** none material. The 3D block proportions are my artistic interpretation of the fact sheet's description (a large red square, small blue square, small yellow rectangle); the fact sheet doesn't give exact pixel ratios, so the 3D canvas is a faithful-in-spirit rendering, not a measured reproduction. The text content is byte-exact to the fact sheet's claims.
